# Performance monitors

E2K cores count hardware events in debug registers that Linux exposes
through perf. Emulators have none of this, so it is the way to see on
hardware what a program's instructions did: how many wide instructions
ran, how many cycles they took, how often the pipeline stalled and why,
DAM and cache behaviour.

Status markers:

- **[source]**: MCST Linux 6.1: `arch/e2k/kernel/perf_event/perf_event.c`,
  `include/asm/perf_event_types.h`, `cpu_regs_types.h`,
  `kernel/hw_breakpoint.c`; event lists in
  `tools/perf/pmu-events/arch/e2k/v3..v7/Events.json` (names, codes and
  Russian descriptions)
- **[hw]**: measured on the Elbrus 4C (elbrus-v3, kernel
  6.1.158-mcst-e4c, perf 6.1.128) by `tools/isa-probes/pmu.c` (loop
  kernels generated by `gen_pmu.py`; the helper is `pmu.h`), and on the
  4C, the 8C2 and the 2C3 by `tools/isa-probes/pmu2.c` (`gen_pmu2.py`:
  every core event of the v3, v5 and v6 lists on 192 loop kernels, one
  event open at a time)

## Registers [source, hw]

| Register | What | User mode |
|---|---|---|
| `%dimcr` | instruction monitor control: per monitor (DIM0, DIM1) `user`, `system`, `trap` (interrupt on overflow) and an 8-bit event number; bit 11 `u_m_en` and bits 12–15 `mode` (the v6 trace's record size, below) (`cpu_regs_types.h:1213-1231`) | `rrd` works. `u_m_en` is not what makes `%dimar` readable: perf never sets it (`perf_event.c:457-462`), and the kernel clears it and `mode` on every switch to a task that is not being traced and at exec (`include/asm/regs_state.h:887-935,1066-1070`, `kernel/process.c:2057-2059`), yet `rrd %dimar0/1` works [source, hw]. ptrace refuses to set it on v6 and later, "Prohibit user changing of monitor registers" (`kernel/ptrace.c:1132-1139`), so it presumably lets user code write the monitors (inferred) |
| `%dimar0`, `%dimar1` | instruction monitor counters | **`rrd` works**: a program can read a running counter without a system call |
| `%ddmcr`, `%ddmar0`, `%ddmar1` | data monitor control and counters (DDM0, DDM1); MMU registers | `mmurr` is SIGILL |
| `%dibcr`, `%dibsr`, `%dibar0–3` | instruction breakpoints (valid and trap bits per breakpoint) and their status | |
| `%dimcr1`, `%dimar2/3`, `%ddmcr1`, `%ddmar2/3` | the third and fourth monitors of each kind | v7 only |

So a v3 core counts at most four events at once: two instruction-side
(DIM0, DIM1) and two data-side (DDM0, DDM1). Which events a monitor can
count is fixed per event.

## Using them through perf [source, hw]

The core PMU is `cpu` (`PERF_TYPE_RAW`). A raw config is `0xMMEE`: `EE`
the event number, `MM` the monitor: 0 DDM0, 1 DDM1, 2 DIM0, 3 DIM1, 4
either DDM, 5 either DIM. Events.json writes each event's allowed
monitors before the colon (`2,3:13` is EXEC on DIM0 or DIM1, config
`0x513`; `0x313` pins it to DIM1). `perf list` on the machine shows the
names (`perf stat -e exec,ticks ./prog`).

On the 4C `perf_event_paranoid` is 2: a user counts its own threads in
user mode only (`exclude_kernel`). That is enough for probes and
benchmarks.

- Counting a region in-process: `perf_event_open` disabled, then ioctl
  RESET/ENABLE/DISABLE and `read` around the code (`pmu.h`,
  `pmu_count`). The ioctl wrappers add a constant (35 instructions, about
  200 cycles); subtract an empty run or difference two lengths.
- Pin an event to DIM0 or DIM1 and read `%dimar0/1` directly
  (`pmu_dimar0`): the deltas match perf's count. The value is the raw
  counter of the CPU the thread runs on, so pin the thread
  (`taskset`).
- Sampling (`perf record -e cpu/event=0x313/u -c PERIOD`) records the
  IP at which the overflow trap was taken: the kernel uses the monitor's
  own address (`dim_ip`, read from `%dimar`) only on CPUs with
  `CPU_FEAT_PRECISE_DIMAR`, v7 and later (kernel
  `arch/e2k/kernel/perf_event/perf_event.c:393-406`) [source]. It
  restarts the counter at −PERIOD, so each interval is the period plus
  what was counted between the overflow and the trap. **Samples lock
  onto short code repeated strictly periodically**: `TICKS` samples of a
  kernel of a few hundred cycles called back to back land unevenly in
  it (isa-score's `validate`: a one-cycle loop read 0.35 to 1.25 cycles
  an iteration depending on the period, while EXEC counts and `%clkr`
  were exact; more samples don't help). A random delay between calls
  removes it (`tools/isa-score/validate/main.c`) [hw: 8C2, 4C]. The kernel throttles to
  `perf_event_max_sample_rate` (100,000 per second on the 4C): a period
  of 1 records 668 of 142,000 instructions, so exact per-instruction
  counts can't come from sampling.
- Where samples land: an EXEC sample is on the instruction itself; a
  `TICKS` or `IB_NO_COMMAND` sample taken during a taken transfer's
  bubble is on the target and, less often, on the next one or two
  instructions. So per-block cycles put a taken `ibranch`'s cost in
  its target block, and per-site taken counts come from EXEC −
  `NO_CT_TAKEN` samples at the transfer (`tools/isa-score/profile.py`).
- Hardware breakpoints (`perf stat -e mem:ADDR:x`) count only the first
  hit after each kernel entry (3 counted for 21 calls): the kernel
  disarms the breakpoint on a hit and re-arms it through a single-step
  that doesn't fire for user code here. Don't use them to count.

## Events checked on the 4C [hw]

Figures per execution of a kernel's loop body, after subtracting an
empty loop (`pmu.c`).

| Event (config) | Counts | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| `TICKS` (0x272) | cycles | `add8`: 8; `nop 7`: 8 |
| `EXEC` (0x313) | wide instructions executed (a `nop N` instruction is 1) | `add8`: 8; `nop 7`: 1 |
| `BUB_B_NOP` (0x21a) | cycles of `nop N` waits | `nop 7`: 7 |
| `BUB_B` (0x219) | cycles phase B is held (nops, stalls) | |
| `BUB_E2` (0x211) | **interlock stall steps; each costs 4 cycles** | `ldd` used 2 cycles early: 1 step, +4 cycles; `muld` used 3 early: 2 steps, +8 |
| `BUB_E2_MEM`, `BUB_E2_ALUn_MEM` (0x230, 0x231…) | steps waiting for a load result | `ld_use`: 1 |
| `BUB_E2_OPND`, `BUB_E2_ALUn_OPND` (0x23c, 0x248…) | steps waiting for an operand, by consumer channel (load results too, below) | `mul_use`: 2 in ALC1 |
| `CONF_ALUn_OUT` (0x240–0x242, 0x350–0x352) | write-back conflicts in ALC n (timing.md) | `muld,0` then `addd,0` 2 cycles later: 1; `addd,2` instead: 0 |
| `IB_NO_COMMAND` (0x218) | cycles without an instruction to issue: taken `ibranch`es (6 each) and taken `ct`s waiting for their CTPR, nothing else in cached code (control-transfer.md, "Instruction fetch") | two taken `ibranch`: 12; a taken `ct` 1 cycle after its `disp`: 3 |
| `NO_CT_TAKEN` (0x220/0x320) | executed instructions without a taken transfer, so EXEC − `NO_CT_TAKEN` = taken transfers (calls and returns count; v6 renames it, below), except around a taken `rbranch`, where it exceeds EXEC | gcc-claude CoreMark: 1.136 G sampled at transfer sites, 1.137 G from `perf stat`; a failed DAM check an iteration (`pmu2.c` `dam_st_same`): EXEC 5, `NO_CT_TAKEN` 7, on all three machines |
| `RBRANCH` (0x217) | taken `rbranch`, both `%MLOCK` and `%dt_al` | failed DAM check: 1; `%dt_al` on a diagnostic: 1 |
| `TRAPS` (0x216) | interrupts | 0 for hardware register-file spills |
| `BUB_B_RF_SPILLFILL` (0x267), `BUB_B_CHAIN_SPILLFILL` (0x266) | register-file and chain-stack spill/fill stalls | 64-deep recursion: about 4 and 2 per level; 2-deep: 0 |
| `DAM_LINE` (0x020) | lock loads entering the DAM | one per lock load |
| `DAM_BELL` (0x120) | checks that failed (`%MLOCK` set) | |
| `DAM_OVFL` (0x121) | lock loads that evicted an entry | 33 locks after a clear: 1; 48: 16 |
| `L1_QUERY` (0x000), `L1_HIT` (0x100), `L1_ST_QUERY` (0x101), `L1_ST_HIT` (0x001), `DTLB_QUERY` (0x010) | L1 and DTLB accesses; `L1_HIT` counts stores that hit as well as loads (v6 swaps 0x001 and 0x101, below; more in "The other events") | one `ldd`: 1 query, 1 hit; a store and a load of its line: `L1_HIT` 2, 1 when the store sends the load to L2 (`damlist.c`; timing.md, "Store to load") |
| `COND_ALU_FALSE` (0x225) | on the 4C **not** what its description says (operations cancelled by their predicate); on v5 and v6 exactly that ("The other events") | 4 per ordinary instruction, 0 for one with four operations predicated off, 5 with one off, 2 with six: unexplained, don't use on v3 |

Also measured with `tools/isa-probes/stbase.c` (pipelined daxpy
kernels and short loops, timing.md "Write-back conflicts"; 4C, 8C2 and
2C3 alike):

- `CONF_ALUn_OUT` counts a conflict whether or not it delays anything:
  a product going to a store, to an FP operation in its own cluster, or
  with time to spare counts too (`plain`, on the 2C3 `l5_plain`;
  `rebased_add2_ch0`, `wb_own_same`: 1.00 an iteration, no stall). A conflict whose
  integer operation waits in a stalled instruction counts once (`wb_*`).
- `BUB_E2_ALUn_OPND` counts load-use waits as well: a load used too
  early (one step) is one step in both `BUB_E2_ALUn_MEM` and `BUB_E2_ALUn_OPND` of
  the consumer's channel, and one in `BUB_E2` (`wb_mid_none`,
  `wb_ld_mid_none`). A store waiting for its base register counts in
  its own channel's, ALU2 or ALU5 (`age_p_m4`, `dr_*`).
- `TICKS_E2` (0x22f/0x32f; v5 and v6 only, perf refuses it on the 4C) counts
  3 per `BUB_E2` step in these kernels, and 4 per step when the stalled
  instruction follows one with `nop 1` (`wb_nop_*`).

Facts these gave about the core (also in the other spec files):

- A stall is a whole number of 4-cycle E2 repeats: the hardware
  mechanism behind timing.md's stall rule.
- The DAM holds exactly 32 entries; a 33rd lock evicts the oldest
  (speculation.md).
- A call deep enough to spill the register file loses DAM entries; a
  shallow call keeps them (speculation.md).
- Register-file and chain-stack spills happen without traps.

## DTLB and AAU events [hw]

Checked by `tools/isa-probes/apbleft.c` `col` and `bk` on the 4C, 8C2
and 2C3: APB loops counted per iteration (apb.md, "Which half an area is
in" and "Plain loads beside an area"); the descriptions are
Events.json's.

| Event (config) | Counts | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| `DTLB_TLU_QUERY` (0x012) | "DTLB accesses from the TLU" (the table-walk unit): one per table walk (inferred) | 1.0 an element of a column walk with a new 4 KiB page each step; 0.01 when the DTLB holds the pages; 0 with 2 MiB pages |
| `TLU_BUSY` (0x112) | cycles the TLU is busy | 11.1, 14.0 and 40.1 a walk on the 4C, 8C2 and 2C3; two walking areas give twice one area's, in either half of the buffer |
| `DTLB_AAU_QUERY` (0x013) | the AAU's DTLB lookups | one per 32-byte line an area fetches (0.25 an iteration for 8-byte elements, 1 an element for a column walk); an area of step 0 one at every step; an area that has stopped fetching 0 |
| `STALL_AAU` (0x113) | stall steps while "decode is blocked by the AAU" | every `BUB_E2` step of a column walk, and of plain loads beside an area |
| `DTLB_HIT` (0x110) | DTLB hits, first pass of each request only | 4C, 8C2: 1 an element of a walking area; 2C3: 0 |
| `DTLB_3_HIT` (0x016) | hits in the large-page entries for the secondary (x86) space's 2/4 MB pages | 0 with native 2 MiB pages, as its description implies |
| `L1_LD_MISS` (0x105, v6) | L1 load misses | 2C3: 0.75 for each 8-byte load of a stream from L2 at II 4; 1 for each AAU load |

## v5 (Elbrus-8C2) [hw]

The events checked on the 4C keep their numbers on v5 (`TICKS` 0x572,
`EXEC` 0x513, `BUB_E2` 0x511, `NO_CT_TAKEN` 0x520, `CONF_ALU0_OUT`
0x540, `DAM_*`, `RBRANCH` 0x517; only `L1_HIT` 0x100 is gone), and the
monitor probe gives the same counts there, so `profile.py` works on v5
unchanged. v5's list (163 core events; `perf list` adds 120 uncore
ones) splits the caches further: `L1_REQUEST` (0x404, either data
monitor; "synchronous requests except qpword"),
`L1_LD_HIT` 0x100, `L1_ST_QUERY` 0x101, `L1_ST_HIT` 0x001, `L2_QUERY`
0x040, `L2_HIT` 0x140, `L2_ST_QUERY` 0x141, and MAU (memory access
unit) and L3 events. They showed that `ldqp` bypasses L1 (timing.md,
"Elbrus-8C2"). With more events than counters `perf stat` multiplexes
and scales the counts; ask for at most four at a time for exact ones.

`L1_LD_HIT` (0x100) counts the loads L1 serves, and `L2_QUERY` (0x040)
every store (L1 is write-through) and every load L2 serves: a store
and a load of another line count 1 `L1_LD_HIT` and 1 `L2_QUERY` a
step, a store that sends the load to L2 0 and 2, and the same store
under a false predicate 1 and 0 (`tools/isa-probes/damlist.c` `t_*`,
8C2 and 2C3; timing.md, "Store to load"). An intact DAM check counts in `L1_QUERY` and
`DTLB_QUERY` but never in `L2_QUERY` (speculation.md).

## v6 (Elbrus-2C3) [hw]

The same event numbers work on the 2C3 (kernel 6.1.0-1.17-e2c3,
`perf_event_paranoid` 2, user-mode counting allowed), so `profile.py`
and `validate.py` run there unchanged (`--cpu 0`: two cores). `pmu.c`
built by the 2C3-tuned lcc gives the 8C2's `TICKS` in 134 of its 166
kernels. Every other one is a load consumed 3 or 4 cycles after it
(`ld_use3_*`, `ld2_*`, `ldstall_*`, `stallnop_*`, `mm_*`, the speculative
`dt_al*`): 4 cycles more, with one more `BUB_E2_MEM` stall step, since a
load takes 5 cycles on v6 (timing.md, "Elbrus-2C3"); besides those, a
`disp` with a false `ct` in its own instruction takes 2 cycles (3), and
64-deep recursion 20 more (1,717), counted as 10 `BUB_B_CHAIN_RET_NRDY`
(returns waiting for the chain stack to be refilled from memory, 0 on
the 8C2) and 23 more `BUB_B_IP_NRDY`. Its spills count as many
`L1_ST_QUERY` as `L1_ST_HIT` there (360), where the 8C2 counts 520
queries for the same 360 hits.

v6 moves and swaps some codes [source: v6 Events.json; hw: `pmu2.c`,
2C3, kernel now 6.1.0-1.18-e2c3]. 0x001 is `L1_ST_QUERY` (one per
store) and 0x101 `L1_ST_HIT`, the reverse of v3 and v5, so `pmu.c`'s
names for the two are swapped on the 2C3 (both read 360 there, so the
figures above stand). 0x000 is `MEM_QUERY` (v3's `L1_QUERY`) and
0x404 `L1_QUERY` (v5's `L1_REQUEST`). 0x520 is renamed `CT_NOT_TAKEN`
("conditional transfers not taken") but counts what `NO_CT_TAKEN`
counts on v3 and v5 (an iteration of `add8` 8, `ct_ct_false` 3,
`ct_ct_taken` 2, `ct_call` 7, identical on all three machines), so
`profile.py`'s EXEC − 0x520 stays right on v6. The new 0x527 `CT_TAKEN` counts the taken
transfers directly: it equals EXEC − 0x520 in every `pmu2.c` kernel
except a system call an iteration (5 against 3) and a failed DAM check
(1 against −2, above).

MCST's kernel lists two errata that bear on measurements (hwbugs.md):
data-monitor events can be lost on the E2S (`KERNEL_DATA_MONITOR`), and
on the 8C2 and the 2C3 the kernel turns the pipeline-freeze feature off
while monitors run (`PIPELINE_FREEZE_MONITORS`).

## The other events [hw: `pmu2.c`, 4C, 8C2, 2C3]

`pmu2.c` counts every core event of the v3, v5 and v6 lists, one at a
time, on 192 loop kernels with known contents, and reports each per
access, line, page or iteration as stated. Three figures are 4C / 8C2 /
2C3; one figure holds on all three. Counts agree within 5% between
runs except the stall-cycle events of streams to memory (about 30%) and
the figures given as ranges, which are the spread of two to four runs.
Quoted descriptions are translated from Events.json.

What the kernel accepts matches its `hw_raw_event_to_iset`
(`perf_event.c:1732-1931`): the v3 list has 162 core events, v5's 163
and v6's 186, as `perf list` shows; the v6-only codes are `EINVAL` on
the 4C and 8C2, and 0x031, 0x032, 0x035 and 0x13a (v3 only) on the 8C2
and 2C3. Three codes in no list are accepted too: DIM 0x14 counts
exactly what `EXEC` counts (196–197 of 197 kernels), and DDM
0x070–0x072 and 0x170–0x172 follow the L2 events 0x040–0x042 and
0x140–0x142, except that 0x070 counts 2.6–3.7 per load that goes to
memory on the 4C and 8C2 (`L2_QUERY` 1). The 4C's `L2_SNOOPM_HIT`
(0x14b, "snoop hits returning modified data") counts cycles: it equals
`TICKS` within 3% in 191 of 197 kernels. perf's `hit_rate` metrics
divide these events (`l1_hit_rate` = `L1_HIT` / `L1_QUERY`,
`l2_hit_rate` = `L2_HIT` / `L2_QUERY`, `dtlb_hit_rate`), so with the
counts below they mislead: `L1_HIT` and `L2_HIT` exceed the accesses,
and on v3 and v5 a DTLB miss counts a hit.

### Instruction fetch

The instruction buffer fetches along two paths, the sequential one
("direct branch": straight code and the target of a taken `ibranch`) and
the prepares' ("preparations": `disp` and the like).

| Event (config) | Counts | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| `IB_AHEAD_QUERY` (0x300) | instruction-cache tag lookups of the sequential path: one per 256-byte line entered | 256, 1,024 and 4,096 bytes of straight code in a loop: 1, 4 and 16 an iteration; a taken `ibranch`: 3 |
| `IB_AHEAD_MISS` (0x301), `IB_AHEAD_MEM_QUERY` (0x309) | lines of the sequential path not in the instruction cache, and their requests to memory (L2) | 256 KiB of straight code: 1.00 per line, both |
| `IB_AHEAD_ITLB_MISS` (0x307) | ITLB misses of the sequential path | a ring of taken `ibranch`es, one per 4 KiB page: 0.02 per page for 128 pages, 0.04 for 256, 1.07 for 384 and 512 |
| `IB_DISP_QUERY` (0x302) | tag lookups of prepares: 3 per prepare of a cached target, whatever its `ipd`; 2 to 3.2 in code that streams from L2 | |
| `IB_DISP_MISS` (0x303), `IB_DISP_MEM_QUERY` (0x30a) | prepared lines not in the cache, and their requests | 256 KiB of straight code with a prepare every fourth line to the line 64 lines ahead: 0 / 1.2 / 2.5 / 3.7 / 3.6–3.7 requests per prepare for `ipd` 0 / 1 / 2 / 3 / no SS, while `IB_AHEAD_MISS` falls from 4 to 3 / 2 / 1 / 1 per 4 lines |
| `IB_DISP_ITLB_MISS` (0x308) | prepares whose target's page misses the ITLB | prepares of targets in 256 KiB of code that never runs: 1.00 per prepare, no request, no DTLB or TLU query (`ib_near_cold`); the same targets once a ring of `ibranch`es has run through their 64 pages: 0, and 0.9–1.5 requests per prepare (`ib_near_warm`) |

So:

- A prepare fetches `ipd` 256-byte lines starting at its target, and a
  prepare without SS 3: the depths control-transfer.md ("Prefetch
  depth") derived from timing.
- A prepare whose target's page is not in the ITLB starts no page walk
  and fetches nothing, whatever its lead.
- The ITLB holds at least 256 and fewer than 384 4 KiB pages. An ITLB
  miss is a page walk through the DTLB: `DTLB_QUERY` and
  `DTLB_TLU_QUERY` 1 per page, `TLU_BUSY` 11 / 14 / 40 cycles per page,
  as for data ("DTLB and AAU events", above).

One count is unexplained: a 144-byte loop of one prefetch in ALC3 a
wide instruction that crosses a 256-byte line (`pf1c3_mem`) counts one
`IB_AHEAD_MISS` and one `IB_AHEAD_ITLB_MISS` an iteration on all three,
at no cost in `TICKS`; the same loop with the prefetch in ALC0, 2 or 5
counts none.

### L1 and DTLB

| Event (config) | Counts | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| `L1_QUERY` (0x000; v6 `MEM_QUERY`), v5 `L1_REQUEST` and v6 `L1_QUERY` (0x404) | every load, store, prefetch and lock load; on v3 and v5 2 for a load that crosses a 32-byte line or a store that crosses a doubleword (v6: 1) | 1.00 per access in every stream; 0.25 per `movad` (one per 32-byte line an area fetches); `loop_mode` stores suppressed by `pcnt` or `strmd` count nothing (8 of 16, [loops.md](loops.md)) |
| `L1_HIT` (v3) / `L1_LD_HIT` (v5, v6) (0x100), `L1_INT_HIT` (0x002) | 1.0 to 1.5 per load that hits L1, unexplained; v3's `L1_HIT` and `L1_INT_HIT` everywhere also count stores (0.1–0.7 per store) | one `ldd` an iteration 1.15 / 1.50 / 1.27–1.35, two 1.00, four 1.22–1.31: not a hit ratio |
| `L1_LINE` (0x003) | lines filled into L1, per access | `ldd` at stride 32 from L2 0.64–0.65 / 0.50 / 0.74–0.75, stride 64 0.50 / 0.50 / 0.25, stride 64 from memory 0.25 / 0.50 / 0.24; a load from memory used at once 2 / 2 / 1; one MAS-0 prefetch a wide instruction 1.2–1.9 / 1.6–1.8 / 0.65–0.76, four 0.16 / 0.26 / 0.09; MAS 0x20 and 0x60 prefetches and stores 0 (timing.md, "Not every load that misses fills L1") |
| v6: `L1_LD_QUERY` (0x005), `L1_LD_MISS` (0x105), `L1_MISS` (0x006), `L1_ST_MISS` (0x103) | as named; prefetches count as loads | |
| v6: `L1_PREFETCH` (0x007), `L1_PREFETCH_MISS` (0x106) | stores, and loads to `%empty` in ALC2 or ALC5 | one per store; a load to `%empty` in ALC0 or ALC3: 0 |
| v5, v6: `L1_LINE_MBF_FULL` (0x102) | L1 fills cancelled because the miss buffer is full | 0.10–0.26 per MAS-0 prefetch in streams of them |
| `DTLB_QUERY` (0x010), `DTLB_HIT` (0x110) | 1 per access; a DTLB miss counts 2 queries and, on v3 and v5, 1 hit | so misses = queries − hits there; v6 counts no hit for a miss and adds `DTLB_LD_MISS`, `DTLB_ST_MISS` and `DTLB_PREFETCH_MISS` (0x11a–0x11c): 1.00 per miss |
| `STALL_DTLB_MISS` (0x017), `STALL_DTLB` (0x111) | E2 stall steps (4 cycles each) for DTLB misses; `STALL_DTLB` all DTLB stall steps (misses, misaligned accesses, lock-wait loads) | per miss: 4.0 / 4.8 / 11.3 |
| `DTLB_SRU_QUERY` (0x011) | the register-file spill and fill unit's accesses | 3.1–3.2 per level of 64-deep recursion, 0 at depth 2 |
| `DTLB_LINE_UNALIGNED` (0x117), `STALL_DTLB_UNALIGN` (0x118) | v3, v5: loads that cross a 32-byte line and stores that cross a doubleword, and their stall steps | `ldd` or `ldw` across a line, `std` or `stw` across a doubleword: 1 each (5 cycles a wide instruction against 1: timing.md, "What costs is crossing a boundary"); inside a line or doubleword: 0. v6's description counts accesses that cross a 4 KiB page instead (not tested); line crossings read 0 there |
| `STALL_DTLB_SEMLOCK` (0x119) | stall steps of lock-wait loads | lcc's fetch-add: 2 / 4 / 2 |

**DTLB reach.** One load per 4 KiB page, cycled over P pages
(`tlb*`), makes no table walks (`DTLB_TLU_QUERY`) for P up to 768,
about 0.5 a load for 896, 0.86–1.00 for 1,024 and 1.00 from 2,048 on:
the 768 entries for 4 KiB pages that apb.md derives from the kernel
("Why": 256 lines of 4, the fourth for large pages). With 2 MiB pages,
4,096 loads over 16 MiB make none. A miss whose page-table entries are
cached costs 15 / 17 / 44–45 cycles (`tlb4096` against `tlb768`),
stores alike, nearly all of it `STALL_DTLB_MISS` steps.

### L2

| Event (config) | Counts | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| `L2_QUERY` (0x040) | requests to L2: each L1 load miss, every store (L1 is write-through: four stores to one line are 4), each prefetch, each 32 bytes of instruction fetch, each AAU fetch; a store that misses L2 is retried (4–36 queries a store) | 1.00 per access; 8 per 256-byte instruction line; 0.25 per `movad` |
| `L2_HIT` (0x140), `L2_ST_HIT` (0x041) | can exceed the queries | about 2 per load at stride 32 over data in L2, 0.95–1.10 at stride 64, 9–10 per instruction line |
| `L2_ST_QUERY` (0x141) | stores, retries included | |
| `L2_LINE` (0x042) | lines allocated in L2: 1 per 64-byte line from memory, for stores too, and for MAS 0 and 0x20 prefetches | MAS 0x40 and 0x60 loads and stores, and MAS 0x60 prefetches: 0 |
| `L2_LINE_DISCARD` (0x142) | 2 for each dirty line written back (twice `MAU_ST_AND_WB` in store streams), 1 per MAS 0x60 store | |
| v6: `L2_LD_QUERY` (0x04d), `L2_MISS` (0x04e), `L2_ST_MISS` (0x14d), `L2_LD_MISS` (0x14e), `L2_PREFETCH_HIT` and `L2_PREFETCH_MISS` (0x04f, 0x14f) | as named; a store miss counts each retry | |
| 8C2: `L2_EXT_QUERY` (0x043), `L2_EXT_INV` (0x143), `MAU_READ_AND_INV` (0x137) | "external (coherent) requests to L2", "external invalidates", "coherent responses": about 1 per line streamed from memory, 0 for MAS 0x60 loads; 0 on the 4C and 2C3, except `L2_EXT_QUERY` 1 per MAS 0x60 store there | presumably the 8C2's L3 invalidating what it evicts (inferred) |
| `L2_TLB_STALL`, `L2_MRQ_STALL`, `L2_WBQ_STALL`, `L2_STMB_HOLD_STALL`, `L2_ARB_BUFF_STALL`, v5 and v6 `L2_STMB_OVERFLOW` (0x045, 0x145, 0x046, 0x146, 0x147, 0x047) | stall cycles, seen in store and prefetch streams to memory | |

### MAU (the memory access unit)

| Event (config) | Counts | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| `MAU_LDB_LINE` (0x033), `MAU_LDB_MERGE` (0x034) | 64-byte lines read from memory, and second requests merged into a pending one | 1.00 per line, store fills and MAS 0x40 and 0x60 loads included; 0.50 per load at stride 32 |
| `MAU_READS` (0x038), `MAU_READ_RI` (0x138) | memory reads: 1 per line on v3 and v5, 1.25–2 on v6 | |
| v3: `MAU_READ_RI_LOCAL`, `MAU_READ_RI_REMOTE` (0x139, 0x13a) | reads served by the local node or another one | the 4C with the data on node 0 / node 1 (`numactl`): 1.00 in the one, 0 in the other; a dependent load costs 100 / 229 cycles |
| v6: `MAU_READ_RAM` (0x139), `MAU_R64_COUNT` (0x03a) | 2 per 64-byte line read (1 for MAS 0x40 and 0x60 loads) | |
| `MAU_ST_AND_WB` (0x136), `MAU_ST_NO_WB` (0x131) | writes to memory: dirty lines written back plus uncached stores; uncached stores alone (MAS 0x60, 1 per store) | |
| `MAU_LDBOVFL_STALL` (0x030); on the 4C also `MAU_QUERY_IN_STALL` (0x035, v3 only) and `MAU_STB_OVFL_STALL` (0x130) | load- and store-buffer overflow stall cycles, in streams to memory | |
| `MAU_ST_NOWB_NOWP` (0x135) | "requests into the store buffer that are neither write-back nor write-protected": on v5 and v6 1 per MAS 0x60 store, 2 per MAS 0x40 store, 2.1–2.6 per plain store to memory; 0 on the 4C | |

A **prefetch with MAS 0x60** makes one L2 query that misses and nothing
else: `MAU_LDB_LINE`, `MAU_READS` and `L2_LINE` are 0, and it issues at
no cost (timing.md, "What each MAS fills").

### Pipeline repeats and the rest

| Event (config) | Counts | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| `BUB_E0` (0x310); v5, v6 `TICKS_E0` (0x32e) | E0 repeats, 2 cycles each | |
| `BUB_E0_USD` (0x362) | a `getsp` 1 or 2 cycles after another (`getsp 0` too): one repeat | +2 cycles; 3 apart: free |
| `BUB_E0_FCMP_CMP` (0x324), `BUB_E0_PU` (0x321) | an FP compare and then an integer compare into predicates in one channel 2 cycles apart: one repeat (v6: one E2 step instead) | +2 (v6 +4); ALC0 and ALC1, or 1 or 3 cycles apart, or the integer compare first: free |
| `BUB_E0_FCMP_CMP2` (0x322) | an FP compare into a predicate in a call's instruction or the one before it, with a compare into a predicate in the callee's first instruction | 26 against 24 cycles a call |
| v6: `BUB_E0_CNTXT_NRDY` (0x361) | 2 per system call | |
| `BUB_E2_SETWD` (0x33b) | a callee's `setwd` that makes the window larger than the caller's waits for every load the thread has outstanding, whatever its destination register; pending divides don't count | a load from memory into the caller's own register, then a call: 68.5 / 104–112 / 112–113 cycles against 27.0 when the callee's window fits in the caller's (10.4 / 21 / 21 steps, also counted in `BUB_E2_OPND`); `sdivd` or `fdivd` pending: 25 either way |
| `BUB_E2_DIV_SQRT1` (0x356) | two divider operations 1 cycle apart: one step | `fsqrts` then `sdivd` 3 cycles later (timing.md, "Divider"), +4 on v3 and v5, counts only in `BUB_E2_ALU345` |
| `BUB_E2_PFPFR_COMB` (0x347) | `rws %pfpfr` in the instruction after a combined FP operation: one step | the reverse, `rws` after `faddd`, and `rrs %pfpfr` after `rws`: free |
| `BUB_E2_ALUn_OPND` | also a late operand of a combined operation (the third one included); `BUB_E2_ALUn_COMB` never counted | |
| `BUB_E2_ALUn_OVFL` (0x337–0x33a) | 0.01–0.36 per load in streams of loads from memory that nothing reads | |
| v5, v6: `TICKS_E2` (0x32f) | cycles of E2 repeats: 3 per step for a load or multiply result (above), 4 for `setwd`, divider and `%pfpfr` steps | |
| v5, v6: `TICKS_LONG_E2` (0x32d) | cycles waiting for a load from memory | 137–157 / 167–185 per load used at once; 0 for `setwd` waits |
| `BUB_B_HWCMD` (0x315) | "hardware commands executed" | 5.5 per level of 64-deep recursion |
| `TICKS_HIDDEN_TRAPS_MASKABLE`, `_UNMASKABLE` (0x373, 0x374) | cycles with interrupts masked | 5 each per system call; `TRAPS` reads 0 for system calls in user-mode counting |
| `HS_SW` (DIM0 only, 0x20f) | executed instructions whose header has the `sw` bit, which `set_mark` sets (bundle.md) | 1 per `set_mark` instruction, else 0 |
| `COND_ALU_FALSE` (DIM0 only, 0x225) | v5, v6: operations cancelled by a false predicate, exactly | 2, 4 and 6 for 2, 4 and 6 operations, loads and stores too; 0 for ordinary instructions and for `loop_mode` stores suppressed by `pcnt`/`strmd`; the 4C's is broken (above) |
| `COND_AM_FALSE` (DIM0 only, 0x226) | never counted | stores and loads under a false predicate, suppressed `loop_mode` stores: 0 |
| `DAM_BELL_STORE_CONFLICT` (0x122) | a check load and a store in one wide instruction whose addresses agree in their low 12 bits ("determined by 12 bits"): the check fails | the same address or 4 KiB apart: `DAM_BELL` 1, `RBRANCH` 1, 27 cycles against 8; the next doubleword, or the store one instruction earlier: no bell ([speculation.md](speculation.md)) |
| `SLT_COUNT` (0x022), `SLT_WAIT_LOCK` (0x023), `SLT_LOCKED` (0x024), `SLT_BUSY` (0x124) | lock-wait loads ("software semaphores") and the cycles their entry spends waiting, locked and busy | lcc's fetch-add: 1; 8 / 16 / 6; 6 / 6 / 8; 18 / 26 / 20 |

`EXEC` − `NO_CT_TAKEN` and v6's `CT_TAKEN` are above ("v6").

## Uncore PMUs and the v6 trace [source, hw]

| Machine | Uncore PMUs (sysfs) | Events in `perf list` |
|---|---|---|
| 4C | `uncore_sic_{0..3}_mcm`, `uncore_ipcc_{0..3}_{0..2}`, `uncore_iocc_{0..3}_{0,1}` | 64: directory hits, misses and retries and memory-controller reads and writes, 16 per node (sysfs adds `phl_errors` and `retry_ops` for the IPCC links, `busy`, `crc_err` and `time_out` for the IOCC ones) |
| 8C2 | `uncore_sic_0_mcm` | 120 (L3, system commutator, DDR, directory) |
| 2C3 | `uncore_hc_0`, `uncore_hmu_0`, `uncore_iommu_0`, `uncore_mc_0`, `uncore_prepic_0`, and `dimtp_trace` | 144 (hc 15, hmu 70, iommu 28, mc 23, prepic 8) |

The sets are the kernel's (`include/asm/perf_event_uncore.h:14-27`).
**None of them counts for a user at `perf_event_paranoid` 2.** The
uncore PMUs are system-wide only (`task_ctx_nr = perf_invalid_context`,
`uncore_sic.c:423,464,576` and the like), their `event_init` refuses
every `exclude_*` bit (`perf_event/uncore.c:151-153`), and counting the
kernel needs paranoid ≤ 1, a CPU-wide event ≤ 0, or `CAP_PERFMON`
(`include/linux/perf_event.h:1432-1446`). On all three machines
`perf_event_open` gives `EACCES` with kernel counting and `EINVAL`
without, on CPU 0 and per task alike (`pmu2 uncore`), and `perf stat -a`
prints `<not supported>` (perf adds `:u`).

`dimtp_trace` (v6 and later, `dimtp_trace.c:586-605`) records a trace
into a perf AUX buffer driven by an instruction monitor (a DIM event and
a period of at least 5), in records of 8 to 256 bytes chosen by
`%dimcr.mode` (`dimtp_trace.c:52-73,377`). It opens per task in user mode on
the 2C3, but one `perf record -e dimtp_trace/event=0x13,mode=2/u -c 1000`
captured no trace data, and the record format is not in the source:
perf's decoder only dumps the words, a set bit 63 starting a record
(`tools/perf/arch/e2k/util/auxtrace.c:469-489`).

## Not checked yet

- What these count: `COND_AM_FALSE`, `MLT_LINE`, `SLT_BELL`, the other
  E0 events (`BUB_E0_FCMP_CHAIN`, `BUB_E0_CALL_BLOCKS_CHAIN`,
  `BUB_E0_TC_NRDY`, `BUB_E0_CNTXT_PIPELINED`, `BUB_B_CNTXT_READ`),
  `BUB_E2_FROM_E0`, `BUB_E2_ALUn_COMB`, `BUB_E2_FPSR_CONF`,
  `BUB_E2_DIV_SQRT2`, the chain-stack events (`BUB_E2_CHAIN_ST_CFLCT`,
  `BUB_E2_CHAIN_SF_NRDY`, `BUB_B_E2_BLOCKS_RET`, `BUB_B_CHAIN_RD_NRDY`),
  `BUB_B_FAPB_CNFLCT`, `BPT0`/`BPT1`, `DTLB_MPTDW_MISS`,
  `DTLB_INVALID_PAGES` (0 for `,sm` loads from address 0), the CLW
  events, and the coherence and store-buffer events (`MAU_INVS`,
  `MAU_STB2LDB_*`, `MAU_STMB_MERGE`, `MAU_LDB_STB_CMP`,
  `MAU_LDB_FOUND_STB`, `MAU_ST_WT`, `MAU_LDB_MERGE2`, `MAU_LDB_HIT`,
  `L2_EXT_READ*`, `L2_WCO_STALL`, `L2_WBC_STALL`, `L2_WBQ_WBC_BUSY`,
  `L2_SNOOP_STALL`, `L2_*FLP`): no `pmu2.c` kernel made them count, and
  two cores sharing data were not tried.
- Why `L1_HIT` and `L2_HIT` exceed the accesses, why a prefetched
  instruction line makes 1.23 `IB_DISP_MEM_QUERY`, why `TICKS_E2` counts
  3 cycles a step for load and multiply waits, and the `pf1c3_mem`
  instruction-fetch counts.
- The ITLB's exact size (256 to 383 pages), and whether `pref` fetches
  code whose page is not in the ITLB.
- Whether an outstanding prefetch (a load to `%empty`) also holds up a
  `setwd` that grows the window.
- `dimtp_trace`'s record format, and why `perf record` captured nothing.
- What the uncore PMUs count: they need root or `perf_event_paranoid`
  ≤ 0.
